dependency_graph.handoff: Factor components Y1-Y4, dimensionless, become weighted ES.
ES area scores, score units, enter heterogeneity description.

assumptions.summary: Abiotic variables proxy poorly known biotic factors.
Unverified reports split evenly and unprocessed reports follow current class shares.
Random effects are independent zero-mean normal.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Exclude malformed dates and pre-September 2019 records.
Image input is 3x96x96; 411 training samples are mentioned.
NASS county bee data are used for local-bee context; task admissibility is warned.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Observable task-to-decision chain may explain relevance.
Operational schedule makes the model actionable.

weaknesses.summary: Training protocol and split details are incomplete.
Perfect-match wording conflicts with two errors and .99 accuracy.
Auxiliary NASS data conflict with the supplied-data boundary.
Hypothetical trajectories do not establish field eradication.
Lambda claim extends beyond displayed grid.
Frequency weights are acknowledged as subjective.

candidate_rule_impacts.action: Start from the concrete institutional task, then let the abstract distribute the deliverables.
Place a local data limitation immediately before the model it motivates.
When distributions disagree, show the mismatch before changing the fusion form.
State the threshold and what new records it admits before reporting the update.
Separate average behavior from site variation before interpreting intervals.
Attach a sensitivity conclusion to its actual tested values and scope.
Keep factor score, mixture/CV, and report-count reconciliation as separate interfaces.
Use distribution shape to justify the fusion interface.
For longitudinal control, retain fixed effects, random effects, covariance, and likelihood as one chain.
Use maps and surfaces when the decision is where, not only how much.
Pair classifier metrics with the channel and evaluation boundary.
Show a score-to-frequency form when the output is an operational schedule.
Plot sensitivity values and decision-relevant metric together.
Name accuracy/AUC as evaluation results and preserve missing split details.
Treat hypothetical intervention curves as scenario evidence.
Record sensitivity grid and the exact conclusion supported by the grid.
Record date/season filters with the biological reason given in the paper.
Bind sample counts to split and preprocessing provenance.
Separate allowed task data from auxiliary external sources.
Declare omitted biotic mechanisms when abiotic proxies drive location predictions.
Make uncertain-status allocation rules explicit before text scoring.
Keep random-effect distribution and independence assumptions next to the likelihood.
Trace headline results back to their metric and scope.
Retain combined-model metrics with the stated comparison denominator.
Translate the schedule plot into an explicit seasonal action.
Metric claims require split, seed, optimizer, and class-balance provenance.
Contradictory accuracy language must remain visible.
Check source restrictions before accepting auxiliary data.
Label hypothetical intervention outcomes as scenarios.
Sensitivity conclusions stop at the displayed parameter grid.
Use conditional examples to expose a decision rule without calling them optimized policies.
Use the abstract as a compact map of distinct deliverables before expanding sections.
Make a stateful threshold/reset rule visible before reporting cadence.
Let the memorandum receive computed outputs as actions with qualifiers.

unresolved_questions: Exact factor extraction/rotation and GMM fitting protocol.
Image/text train-test split, optimizer, seed, and calibration.
Whether external NASS data are admissible under the official C task boundary.
How hypothetical eradication curves map to field confirmation.
